newsitem.title: UK: VLCCs active, rates steady on plentiful tonnage.
newsitem.headline: VLCCs active, rates steady on plentiful tonnage.

text.p: The very large crude carrier (VLCC) market was active on Wednesday but rates from the Middle East and West Africa were steady as tonnage was fairly plentiful, brokers said.
"There's quite a lot of tonnage around. If activity continues like this we will see rates starting to rise, but that may not happen till next week," one broker said.
The 275,000 tonne Argo Athena was fixed at W52.5 Mideast/USG for Chevron, loading April 25, while voyages to Singapore fetched about W60 and to Japan W62.5/65.
West Africa/USG VLCCs continued to be fixed at about W70, with 130,000 tonne cargoes steady at W97.5.
"West African activity is picking up after the Easter break but not enough so far to push rates up," another broker said.

The cross-Mediterranean market was quiet with 80,000 tonne rates steady from Tuesday at W125/130 but slightly softer than last week when they hit W140. Cross-Med 130,000 tonne cargoes edged down to W95, and an Italian broker said they could fall further if the current lack of enquiry continued.
The inter-U.K./Cont sector was little changed at W125/130, while 25,000 tonne fuel oil rates were likewise steady at W200 inter-U.K./Cont and W210 cross-Med, brokers said.
In the Western Hemisphere, the spectacular rise in 70,000 tonne crude cargoes showed signs of levelling off with Caribs/upcoast fixtures at W230/235, some five points down from Tuesday.

"I think rates will be getting softer over the next week unless the river problem continues," said a U.S. broker, referring to a blockage caused by a bulk carrier that lost power and struck a dock in the Mississippi.
Current Caribs/upcoast crude rates are almost 100 points above the February average, according to data on Rigos Chartering Inc's Internet site.
Caribs/U.S. 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes edged down to W210/215 from W225.
